I tried to break it in the places the rule's edges are: `skills` with no flags surveyed both destinations, named which copies differ, refused without a terminal (exit 2) and wrote nothing - including against a personal directory that did not exist, which it did not create; `--project` from `deep/nested/` still chose the ROOT copy; `--project` outside a repository refused with exit 2 rather than guessing. I also checked n-0197's remedy is in place: this checkout's own `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` are real files now, not symlinks into `lib/skills/`, so `skills --project --force` here can no longer write through to the shipped sources; I did not run --force in this checkout to avoid touching source either way.
